top_choice_rationale: I rank P001 (Can Xue) first on literary grounds. Under the common criteria, her voice is hard to mistake for anyone else's. Her formal achievement is a dream logic kept as a working principle that replaces conventional psychology, space and causal plot, rather than decorating them. That gives the fiction imaginative and intellectual depth, and the method has been pursued over decades. A single-writer citation resting on the fiction fits, because the contribution is one personal narrative method. The judgment is close and provisional. I rely on public knowledge and translated selections, and I have not independently verified any text. I cannot judge the Chinese prose, and only part of a large output is available in translation. The open question is whether the method shows sustained invention or repetition across the later novels. This remains unanswered, and it is the main condition that could reverse my order. I rank P002 (Cărtărescu) second as a serious and well-grounded alternative, with a citation centred on the novels. The same repetition-versus-architecture test applies to his late long volumes, and his poetry is thinly covered in what I can assess. Both proposals are single-writer and within the protocol's scope. I rank P000 last because the round-2 exchange produced two substantively argued candidates and no case that neither meets the standard of Nobel's will. Agreement among colleagues is not independent evidence, since we share the same translated sample, and I did not use the opening or round-2 support counts as a reason for my ranking.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. The profile records no documented tie to Can Xue or Cărtărescu. My non-fiction practice, my marriage to Pär Nuder and my Wallenberg and Nobel biographies are context only. As Permanent Secretary I may be expected to announce the laureate, but that is not a tie to any candidate. My simulated vote is a modeling assumption, because the voting status of a co-opted member is undocumented. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
